newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end mixed but downtrend intact.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end mixed but downtrend intact.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended mixed Friday, on reasonable volumes, as some end-of-week short covering helped to keep both December gold and silver above Thursday's lows.

"You'd have to say the longer term trend was still down, with any lack of momentum today not surprising on a Friday, and support in gold probably somewhere down in the low $370's," Imperial Bank's California-based chief bullion dealer Jeff Singer said.
COMEX December gold ended up 10 cents at $379.20 an ounce, after trading in a $379.50-377.80 range.

In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $378.00/378.50 an ounce, compared to the London Friday afternoon fix at $377.60 and the New York close Thursday at $377.50/378.00, after spot gold saw its lowest levels since March 1995 this week at $376.70.
The spot gold/silver ratio ended little changed at 78.8, after climbing sharply in the past few weeks to a new 18 month high at 78.0, as silver led the complex down.
COMEX December silver closed down 1.0 cent at $4.798, after trading a $4.815-4.765 range.
Fresh U.S. economic data Friday, including October non-farm payrolls, October unemployment, and the September leading indicator, suggested inflation remained little threat, analysts said.
Meanwhile the strength of the US dollar, which saw a 42 month high gainst the yen this week, was depressing demand for precious metals in jewelry and industry in Japan.

Open interest in COMEX gold futures rose 4,874 lots Thursday, in data released Friday, suggesting funds were adding to short positions while commercials were hedging against further prices declines, traders said.
Short term implied gold lease rates climbed sharply to around 2.50 percent Friday, suggesting further speculative shorting in the bullion market, analysts said.

The COMEX December/April contango continued to narrow, ending at $4.00 an ounce Friday, from a high of $5.50 in early June, and the 12 month December 1996/December 1997 contango fell to $12.30 an ounce, the lowest level since February, with some producer hedging noted this week also.
But technical indicators for December gold, such as a standard nine-day relative strength indicator (RSI), were beginning to look oversold at 26 percent at the close Friday.
Spot silver bullion fell to a low of $4.76 an ounce this week, its lowest level since March 1995, though COMEX silver stocks fell to a fresh 10 year low at 130,028,540 ounces.

NYMEX January platinum ended up 70 cents at $384.80 an ounce, but not before seeing a fresh life-of-contract low at $383.00 early. Cash market platinum fell to a low of $370.00 this week, its lowest levels since January 1994.
NYMEX December palladium ended down 25 cents at $116.50 an ounce, while spot palladium saw fresh three-and-a-half year lows at $114.00 this week.
--Clive Mckeef, New York Commodities 212-859-1641; email: clive.mckeef@reuters.com
